items.body:
## Problem

`SignedArtifact::check()` (the verification gate behind `verify()` and `ArtifactLog::insert`) validates the `after` causal frontier only for count and shape — never for duplicates:

- `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs:280-287` — `after.len() <= MAX_AFTER` (32) and every entry `is_hash(...)`. Nothing rejects the same hash appearing twice.
- The sibling type for the identical concept refuses it explicitly: `ChainExt::validate()` in `pkgs/id/src/chain.rs:187-193` caps `after`, then builds a `HashSet` and returns `ChainError::DuplicateAfter` ("after names the same hash twice", chain.rs:53-55) when a hash repeats. `ChainExt.after` is documented as "the author's causal frontier … At most [`MAX_AFTER`] hashes, none repeated" (chain.rs:104-107).

So a signed artifact whose `after` is `[h, h]`, or even the same hash repeated 32 times — filling the entire frontier with ONE distinct artifact — verifies and is stored by `ArtifactLog`, while an event header carrying the same frontier is refused at decode.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 236cb985)

Laptop probe `probe-2026-10-31-laneA-dupafter` (in `~/git/fleet/` on the laptop) driving the real `id` crate (`SignedArtifact::sign_after` → `verify()` → `ArtifactLog::insert`), `artifact.rs` sha256 `bdc11bbe0cafa72c4017df93523699cad99303520b65c71365e1ca7d3e1bc86b` matched on both clones:

```
control distinct [h1,h2]: verify=Ok(()) insert=Ok(New)
duplicate [h1,h1]: verify=Ok(()) insert=Ok(New)
duplicate x32 (whole frontier, 1 distinct): verify=Ok(()) insert=Ok(New)
duplicate x33 (over cap): verify=Err(an artifact names at most 32 artifacts before it) insert=Err(same)
control distinct x32: verify=Ok(()) insert=Ok(New)
```

Controls show the existing checks work: 32 distinct hashes pass, and 33 entries are refused for count — but the count is spent by duplicates, so the "32 artifacts" the frontier claims to name can be as few as 1.

## Why it matters

- `after` is signed ordering evidence: the module doc (artifact.rs:11-13) says a receiver can order concurrent statements by it and "enforcing that order is up to the consumer". A frontier that repeats one hash is ambiguous evidence — a consumer counting distinct dependencies, or checking whether a specific set was seen, reads a padded list as more causal history than exists.
- The cap's intent is per distinct artifact: `MAX_AFTER` bounds how many artifacts one statement may name. Duplicates spend the budget without naming more, so the same statement can simultaneously satisfy `len == 32` (maximally "informed") and name a single predecessor.
- Cross-type drift: two signed frontier types in one crate enforce different rules for the same field name and concept, so a statement can be valid as an artifact and invalid as an event for the same reason. The chain side already decided the rule — repeated hashes are an error, not a normalization case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SignedArtifact::check()` (or `ArtifactLog` insert) refuses an artifact whose `after` names the same hash twice, with an error naming the duplication.
- [ ] Regression tests: `[h, h]` refused; the same hash ×32 refused; 32 distinct hashes still accepted; over-cap still refused.
- [ ] `sign_after` (the local signing path) refuses or dedupes a repeated `after` hash so a local author cannot mint an artifact remote peers will refuse — signing and verification apply the same rule, as `ChainExt`'s builder/decoder pair does (chain.rs:174-176).
- [ ] Existing artifact tests (paging, sync, directory application) still pass.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for artifact `after` duplicates / `DuplicateAfter` before filing: no existing issue covers the artifact side. Distinct from #3146 (friend_remove `requests` validation), #3187 (home_declared `world_id`), #3192 (document/tag NFC) — different field and rule; this one is the envelope-level `after` check in `check()`, not a `parsed()` kind arm.

items.body:
Design the durable encoding for checkpointed live sessions — the input everything else in the #2034 family depends on.

## Why

[#2034](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2034) investigation (doc: `doc/2026-10-29T10-45-00Z_investigation_ephemeral_live_data_retention/`) concluded on a two-tier model: durable facts stay on the per-author signed hash chain (`ChainExt`), keystroke/cursor/input traffic moves to an ephemeral per-session stream authenticated by a session header + per-session MAC key, closed by intermittent **segment checkpoints**. Nothing in the tree defines what a session header or a checkpoint *is*.

## Scope

- Define `SessionHeader` and `SegmentCheckpoint` records and a new `ChainExt.kind` (`session.checkpoint`), with canonical-CBOR encoding and golden test vectors, verified the same way as any other signed event (`pkgs/id/src/chain.rs:282-342`).
- Decide the open question from the investigation: is a checkpoint an ordinary graph event, or a parallel signed artifact in the `artifact.rs` shape referenced from the graph? State the trade-off and pick one.
- Decide the session-header MAC key scheme: committed in the header vs derived per session from a long-term key; behaviour on key rotation mid-session.
- Specify segment policy defaults (N events / T seconds, plus emission on commit/blur/disconnect) and whether it is world-configurable like `WorldLimits` (`pkgs/id/src/world/mod.rs:59-99`).
- Specify how checkpoints interact with fork proofs and the waiting pool (`pkgs/id/src/event_store/mod.rs:12-22`, `waiting.rs`) so a later compaction cannot break `after` resolution.
- Peer countersignature (`peer_signature`) variant: which classes must require it (#2037/#2038 consume this).

## Acceptance

- A design doc under `doc/` linked from this issue with the record shapes, encoding, verifier walk, and the decisions above.
- Wire fields and a verifier algorithm concrete enough that the PoC issue can be built from it without further design.
- No permanent feature built here — this is design only.

Refs #2034, #2056.

items.body:
Filed by queue triage task 6875 (2026-11-03) from the design record on main, `doc/2026-11-01_design_id2031.md` §2, which names this as "a prerequisite missing from #3788–#3790's current dependency graph" — it has no issue of its own, so the gap is invisible to the fleet.

## The gap (per the design record, verified against main 2026-11-03)

- `ChainExt` carries a free-string `kind` and optional group (`pkgs/id/src/chain.rs`, root `id` package), and the signed header commits to a body's hash and size while the body itself is separate.
- Ingest accepts and verifies a supplied body (`pkgs/id/src/event_store/ingest.rs`), but `store_event` writes `event.bytes` (the signed header) only (`pkgs/id/src/event_store/mod.rs`); range sync sends stored events and fork-proof headers (`pkgs/id/src/event_store/sync.rs`).
- Consequence: a `didit.*` CBOR body can be validated at ingest but is not yet available for later retrieval or cross-device replication.

## Scope

Design + implement generic application event-body persistence, retrieval, and range-sync in `pkgs/id` (not didit-specific), so any `kind` with a CBOR body — starting with the four `didit.*` kinds from issue #3788 — round-trips: stored at ingest, retrievable by event id/hash, and carried by range sync with the same integrity checks as headers.

## Acceptance

- A stored event with a generic body can be retrieved byte-identically after restart.
- Range sync between two nodes transfers bodies for events the peer lacks, with hash/size verification against the signed header.
- Existing header-only kinds are unaffected; tests cover body-present and body-absent events.

## Relations

- Blocks the app phase: issue #3790 (Phase 3 of #2031) cannot read tracker state back without this.
- Does NOT block issue #3788 (Phase 1: library-only schema types + pure evaluator, golden tests only).
- Parent: issue #2031.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generic event-body persistence exists for `pkgs/id`: bodies can be stored, retrieved by event id, and range-synced without per-type bespoke code.
- Retrieval of a missing body returns a typed not-found (not a panic or silent empty).
- Range-sync is idempotent: re-syncing a range does not duplicate bodies.
- Covered by tests exercising persistence, retrieval, and a repeated range-sync.

items.body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #3231 — "a signed artifact is validated as strictly as it is built: one receipt contract for pkgs/id artifacts" (design doc: `files/designs/code-id-artifact-receipt-validation.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace). Filed by design-architect pass 28 (2026-10-31); **gated on Phases 1–2 of #3231 landing** (Phase 1: #3196 + #3146, list integrity; Phase 2: #3192 + #3187, text fields).

## Scope

Build the field-by-field disposition table for `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs`: every field of every known kind (`friend_remove`, `home_declared`, `document`, `tag`) plus every envelope field (`author`, `seq`, `prev`, `kind`, `body`, `after`, `hash`, `signature`), set against the producer or sibling-validator rule that governs it (`directory.rs` producers, `documents.rs` `DocumentRef::check`, `tag_claims.rs` `check_text`, `chain.rs` `ChainExt::validate`, `world_hub.rs` `validate_world_name`). Each field is dispositioned in the closing evidence:

- (a) enforced at receipt — name the check in `check()`/`parsed()` and the phase that landed it, or
- (b) deliberately unvalidated — with the one-line reason, or
- (c) a gap the phases missed and rule 1 of #3231 covers — file it as a named follow-up and link it here; do not fix it inside this audit.

## Explicit dispositions required

- **The `kind` string** of unknown kinds: length/NFC bounds (chain kinds are 1..=MAX_KIND_BYTES and NFC) versus the module's stored-but-never-applied forward-compatibility rule for future kinds. Decide and record the trade.
- **`document.content` internal strings**: `chain.rs` `check_value` requires NFC for every text string including map keys; the artifact document rule governs only `media_type` (the `documents.rs` precedent). Disposition whether content text is governed data or opaque payload.
- **`prev`'s shape** beyond the chain-position equality `ArtifactLog::store` already enforces.
- **Full builder-side symmetry**: `documents.rs`/`chain.rs` builders apply their checks at build time; artifact `sign` is generic over kind strings including future kinds. Record whether `sign` should run `parsed()` for known kinds, with the reasoning (Phase 1 pins only the duplicate-`after` refusal in `sign_after`).
- **`world_id` charset evidence**: gather how `ArtifactLog::declared()` consumers resolve a `world_id` to a served world (the design doc's open question — `validate_world_name`'s `a-z0-9-_` versus `WorldCore::new`'s any-non-blank rule). Record the evidence here; pinning the charset, if warranted, is a follow-up filed from this audit, not a fix inside it.

## Contract statement

Write the #3231 rule into the `artifact.rs` module doc — the builder/decoder symmetry sentence `documents.rs` and `chain.rs` already carry, in artifact terms: a signed artifact is validated at receipt (`check()` + `parsed()`) against every rule its producers and the crate's sibling validators obey; a signed list names each thing once; text fields follow the crate's text rules. Note the unknown-kind exception in the same paragraph.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Disposition table posted on this issue (or a linked PR): every known-kind field and envelope field with a disposition (a)/(b)/(c)
- [ ] The five explicit dispositions above are each recorded with their reasoning
- [ ] Any (c) follow-ups filed and linked; no fixes landed inside this audit issue itself
- [ ] Contract statement landed in the `artifact.rs` module doc; design issue #3231 closed with a link to this evidence
- [ ] This phase did not start before #3231 Phases 1–2 landed (record their closing state in the evidence)

items.body:
Design-architect pass 28 (2026-10-31), audit at origin/main `357ec7fb`. Full design doc: `files/designs/code-id-artifact-receipt-validation.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. NO `user/review` — every origin carries explicit acceptance with verified probe evidence, and the judgment calls below are the architect's recorded decisions.

## Problem

`pkgs/id` has three signed-statement types, and two state the same contract in their docs — `documents.rs`: *"The builder and the decoder both apply them, so a signed document always passes them on receipt"*; `chain.rs` (`ChainExt::validate`): the same sentence for signed events. The third type, artifacts (`pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs`), never applied it to itself: its receipt gates `check()` (envelope) and `parsed()` (the four known kinds) each enforce some of the rules the crate's own producers and sibling validators obey and silently omit others — one omission per field, filed one at a time. Four filings in two days (three in the hours after pass 27 assessed #3146 as a single): #3146 (`friend_remove.requests` never inspected), #3187 (`home_declared.world_id` only `is_empty`-checked; duplicate endpoints pass), #3192 (`document`/`tag` text accepts non-NFC every sibling path refuses), #3196 (`check()` accepts a duplicated `after` frontier `chain.rs` refuses as `DuplicateAfter`).

## The rules (recorded decisions)

1. **Receipt is construction.** `parsed()` refuses a known-kind body no in-tree producer could build; `check()` refuses an envelope no legitimate signer could build — `Refusal::Forbidden` naming the rule, existing per-arm style. Unknown kinds untouched (stored, never applied, envelope-only — the module's deliberate forward-compatibility rule).
2. **A signed list names each thing once.** Duplicates refused, never silently deduped on receipt (the signed bytes are evidence; rewriting falsifies them and breaks the hash). Covers `after`, `friend_remove.requests`, and `home_declared` servers by endpoint. `sign_after` refuses a duplicated `after` at build time — the builder/decoder symmetry the sibling types document.
3. **Text in a signed body follows the crate's text rules.** `document.media_type`, `tag.name`, `tag.value` must be NFC via the same `unicode_normalization::is_nfc` the three sibling validators import. `world_id` gets `MAX_WORLD_ID_BYTES = 64` (aligned with `MAX_WORLD_NAME_BYTES`): 1–64 bytes, not whitespace-only, no control (Cc) or format (Cf) characters.

Field pins: `requests` ≤ `MAX_FRIEND_REQUESTS = 3` (the sole producer `Directory::friendship_requests`, directory.rs:1710–1721, structurally builds at most 3, sorted+deduped), each entry exactly 32 lowercase hex characters (the envelope-ID shape), no duplicates. Junk `requests` entries are not inert — `Directory::apply` extends the permanent `removed_requests` void guard with every string (directory.rs:1698–1705).

## Phases (adopt the origins — no parallels)

- **Phase 1 — List integrity:** #3196 + #3146.
- **Phase 2 — Text fields:** #3192 + #3187. Independent of Phase 1.
- **Phase 3 — Closing audit + contract statement:** filed this pass as a sub-issue, gated on Phases 1–2 (`status/blocked`). Field-by-field disposition table for every known-kind and envelope field; must explicitly disposition the `kind` string (unknown kinds), `document.content` internal strings, `prev`'s shape beyond `store()`'s position check, and full builder-side symmetry; writes the contract sentence into the `artifact.rs` module doc, where `documents.rs`/`chain.rs` already carry it.

## Alternatives rejected (in the doc)

Fixing the four independently (rules diverge — the drift is how the family arose: the artifact arms already mirror the sibling *caps* while missing the NFC half); validating at application time instead of `parsed()` (the log would still store and serve junk; `parsed()` is the single gate insert/open/pull all pass); normalizing on receipt (breaks hash/signature — refusal is the only honest outcome); folding into #3068 (JS/TS shape contract — different gate, different failure mode; cross-referenced, neither gates the other — this answers #3187's triage note); pinning the full `a-z0-9-_` world-name charset for `world_id` now (`WorldCore::new` accepts any non-blank ID — charset stays an open question, below).

## Risks (in the doc)

`ArtifactLog::open()` replays through the same gates, so tightened rules apply to stored chains — legitimate chains unaffected (no producer emits these shapes), refusal-on-open with the line named is existing behaviour; `MAX_FRIEND_REQUESTS = 3` is a producer invariant (constant and producer change together); Cf refusal in `world_id` is safe for machine-chosen IDs (`"home"`/`"lobby"` today).

## Open questions (in the doc, never as issues)

`world_id` charset (`validate_world_name`'s `a-z0-9-_`?) — needs evidence of how `declared()` consumers resolve it; `document.content` internal text NFC (chain's all-text rule vs the `documents.rs` media-type-only precedent); unknown-kind `kind`-string bounds vs forward compatibility; full builder symmetry for `sign`. The neighbouring plain-output rendering family (#2839, #3111, #3089, `world/util.rs` sanitizers) governs *printing* untrusted text, not storing it — not adopted; #3187's Cf pin is deliberately aligned with it.



## Acceptance criteria

- Phase 1 (adopting #3196 + #3146) and Phase 2 (adopting #3192 + #3187) land under the recorded rules: receipt (`check()` / `parsed()`) refuses with `Refusal::Forbidden` any envelope or known-kind body no in-tree producer could build; duplicates are refused, never silently deduped on receipt.
- The Phase 3 closing audit completes the field-by-field disposition table (including `kind`, `document.content` internal strings, `prev` shape, builder-side symmetry) and writes the receipt contract sentence into the `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs` module docs, alongside `documents.rs` / `chain.rs`.
- No legitimate producer output is refused: existing stored artifact chains replay through `ArtifactLog::open()` unchanged.

items.body:
# id(issuer-rotation): `fold_rotation_chain` dedups candidates by event id only — duplicate-id entries with a different author/body make the fold input-order dependent, contradicting its determinism contract

## Evidence (verified this run against main `af0847d00a2231c71f6ebb59eba4cc7db197599e`, via `gh api` raw reads; laptop unreachable this run)

`pkgs/id/src/issuer_rotation.rs:497` documents the fold's core contract:

> The fold is deterministic and independent of input order.

The candidate reduction at `pkgs/id/src/issuer_rotation.rs:560-561` does not uphold it:

```rust
candidates.sort_by_key(|(_, event_id, _)| *event_id);
candidates.dedup_by_key(|(_, event_id, _)| *event_id);
```

`sort_by_key` is stable and `dedup_by_key` keeps the *first* of each equal-key run, so when the input slice contains two entries with the **same event id but different rotation bodies**, whichever entry happens to be listed first survives dedup, and the surviving entry alone decides the generation transition (or the fork resolution) afterwards. The filters at lines 543–559 do not save this: they validate each entry on its own merits, and two *distinct, individually valid* bodies can share one event id in the fold's input. Concretely, this changes the folded result under a mere permutation of the same input multiset:

- Same event id, two valid `Routine` bodies by the current generation key naming **different successor keys** (each correctly countersigned by its own successor). Both pass every filter. Listed A-first, generation *g+1*'s key is A's successor; listed B-first, it is B's — instead of the `ChainStatus::Conflicted` the design (§3.2 rule 5) prescribes for two valid transitions claiming the same predecessor.
- Same event id, one valid `Routine` body and one valid `CompromiseRecovery` body (recovery key author). The survivor decides whether the step is a plain advance or a recovery advance with a `RecoveryStep` recorded — purely by input order.

In the production path the event id is the hash of the signed header, so two *decoded events* cannot collide this way today. But `fold_rotation_chain` is a public, documented-as-order-independent pure function over caller-supplied `(author, event_id, rotation)` tuples — its callers supply authors and rotations extracted from events (`fold_rotation_chain` docs, lines 490–496), and any future caller that merges rotation sets from two sources (store + sync feed, journal replay + live) can present the same id twice with divergent extracted fields. The sibling currency fold had exactly this bug class and it was treated as a real defect: #4069 (closed) — "fold_authorisation duplicate highest version folds by input order — no deterministic tie-break". This fold's contract is stronger (it promises order independence outright) and its reduction is weaker (id-only).

## Why it matters

- The fold is the authoritative answer to "which key speaks for generation *g*" for a currency issuer. An order-dependent fold means two replicas folding the same rotation set can disagree on the active issuer key — the exact failure the module exists to prevent (§3.2 rule 5 refuses arrival-order tie-breaks for the same reason).
- The gap is invisible to the current test suite: every fold test passes distinct event ids (`event(1)`, `event(2)`, …), so no test exercises a duplicate id with divergent fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fold_rotation_chain` returns the identical `GenerationChain` for every permutation of the same input multiset, including inputs containing duplicate event ids whose author or rotation body differ. (Deterministic rule for duplicates: e.g. dedup on the full `(event_id, author, rotation)` tuple with a total order over the tuple, or refuse/ignore all-but-one by a content-derived order — any rule that is a function of the multiset, not of the listing order.)
- A property test (per the repo testing doctrine: the oracle is permutation invariance of the fold) shuffles inputs — including duplicate-id/divergent-field entries — and asserts identical output; it fails on the current code and passes after the fix.
- Existing `issuer_rotation` tests still pass (`cargo test -p id --lib issuer_rotation` on the laptop or CI per house rules).
- Dedup behaviour for the ordinary duplicate case (identical tuples listed twice) is unchanged: the transition still counts once.

items.title: id(chat-presence): heartbeat typing list is never deduplicated or bounded — one channel yields a 3.3 MB signed frame, defeating MAX_HEARTBEAT_CHANNELS

items.body:
## Summary

`pkgs/id` chat presence bounds a heartbeat's `channels` list but not its `typing` list: `typing` is documented as a subset of `channels` ("The channels the node is currently typing in. A subset of `channels`", chat_presence.rs:107-109), yet neither the constructor, the table's receive path, nor the codec deduplicates or caps it. A heartbeat can carry an unbounded number of duplicate typing entries, so one signed heartbeat produces an arbitrarily large gossip frame and an arbitrarily large stored table entry — defeating `MAX_HEARTBEAT_CHANNELS`, whose stated purpose is to "bound the frame size and the work a single received heartbeat can make the table do" (chat_presence.rs:76-78).

## Evidence (verified this run, main 70a595a7)

- `PresenceHeartbeat::new` (chat_presence.rs:138-161) deduplicates `channels` and truncates it to `MAX_HEARTBEAT_CHANNELS` (64), but for `typing` it only filters to entries present in `channels` — duplicates survive and there is no length cap.
- `PresenceTable::update_at` (chat_presence.rs:296-301), the receive path, applies the same filter-only treatment to a decoded heartbeat's `typing`; heartbeats decoded from the wire never pass through `new`, so the constructor's invariants would not save this path anyway.
- The production receiver in `serve` (commands/serve.rs:1575-1591) verifies the signature and then calls `recv_presence.update(heartbeat)`. Signature verification does not help here: the sender signs its own bloated heartbeat with its own key, so `verify()` passes.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-presencetyping/` (verbatim `chat_presence.rs`, md5 68590664a175bd4a17937c28a2f0fb6b, matching sandbox main 70a595a7; minimal stubs for `groups::GroupView` / `waiting::AuthorKey`):
  - `PresenceHeartbeat::new(node, vec![chan], vec![chan; 100_000], ts)` → `channels.len() = 1`, `typing.len() = 100_000`, `encode_frame(...).len() = 3_300_087` bytes (~3.3 MB frame naming one channel).
  - Control: `new` with 500 distinct channels → `channels.len() = 64` (the cap works for channels).
  - A wire-shaped heartbeat with `typing = vec![chan; 50_000]` round-trips through `encode_frame`/`decode_frame` at full length and is accepted by `update_at`.

## Why it matters

Presence is an unauthenticated-reach, always-on gossip surface: any peer on the topic can get its own heartbeats accepted. The one size bound the protocol declares (64 channels) can be bypassed by three orders of magnitude through the sibling field, inflating every receiver's stored entry (retained until the TTL prune) and every re-gossiped frame. It is also a shape bug independent of size: duplicate typing entries mean the stored heartbeat's `typing` is not the set the docs promise, so any future consumer that iterates or counts it inherits the duplicates.

## Acceptance criteria

- `PresenceHeartbeat::new` deduplicates `typing` (after filtering to `channels`), so `typing.len() <= channels.len()` for every constructed heartbeat.
- `PresenceTable::update_at` applies the same dedup/bound to decoded heartbeats, so a wire heartbeat with duplicate or excess typing entries is stored in bounded form (or refused), regardless of the constructor.
- Regression tests: a heartbeat built or decoded with duplicate typing entries (e.g. 100_000 copies of one channel) is stored/encoded with at most one entry per channel; existing chat_presence tests keep passing.
- The bound is stated next to `MAX_HEARTBEAT_CHANNELS` so the frame-size guarantee covers the whole heartbeat, not just `channels`.

Distinct from: #2809 (the presence protocol itself, closed — this is a residual bound gap in its merged implementation), #3927 (abuse evaluator oversize, different module), #3950 (chat v1 core remainder — membership/store/rate, not presence frame bounds).

items.body:
Sibling of #7016 (which covers open-issue↔queue coverage and the done-task-only class). This issue governs the mirror audit Drew ordered 2026-11-07 20:40 CST after the 766 verification found only 8 of 766 "done" tasks were truly done: **double-check every closed issue and PR, and verify each unmerged branch with commits and unpushed worktrees.**

## First-tranche results (2026-11-07 evening, read-only audit)

Evidence file: `~/workspace/scratch/closure-audit-2026-11-07.md` (fleet-local).

**Part 1 — closed issues.** Totals: code 2,612 closed issues / opencode 939 / openchamber 845 / darwin-nix 840 (5,236). Verified the 200 most-recently-closed per repo tranche (darwin 60, openchamber 60, opencode 40, code 40) at the 766's evidence standard:
- 183/200 (91.5%) LEGITIMATE-LINKED (merged PR or closing commit on the timeline).
- 10/200 NO-EVIDENCE by linkage — all 10 read individually: **10/10 legitimate-by-record** (the closure evidence lives in agent-note comments: done-notes citing merge commits, supersession records, decommission records). Confirmed wrongful closures in the tranche: **0**.
- 7/200 DISPOSITION (not_planned/duplicate — incl. 4 "Scheduled Bolt" bot issues).
- Merged-PR "Fixes #N" spot check: 12/12 claimed targets actually closed, no negation traps.
- Closed-unmerged PRs: 326 total (code 206, darwin 55, opencode 39, openchamber 26). Sample of 12 most-recent per repo set: **12/12 closed as superseded/duplicate with a salvage note naming the canonical merged PR.** Zero silently abandoned in sample.

Methodological finding: linkage-only verification UNDERCOUNTS legitimacy — fleet closures carry their evidence in comments, not GitHub linkage. Remainder verification must read the record, not just the timeline.

**Part 2 — unmerged branches.** Remote branches: code 1,702 / opencode 322 / openchamber 221 / darwin 46. From the laptop primaries post-fetch, remote-tracking branches not merged into main: **196, all of them `archive/janitor-2026-11-07/*`** (the disk janitor's by-design archives; 0 non-archive). Local unmerged branches: nix 31 non-archive (mostly `queue/*` task branches, Nov 2–4), opencode ≥48 non-archive, code primaries hit the 100-branch listing cap with archives — full local census remains. Local "unmerged" overstates stranding (squash/merge-commit landings leave local branches permanently unmerged by SHA); patch-equivalence review is the real test.

**Part 3 — worktrees.** Laptop: 67 clone/worktree dirs scanned at ~/git top level + primaries. Named substantive holds:
- `~/git/wt-atlas-snowflake-swap` (feat/atlas-snowflake-production): 6,120 commits not in fork main; `~/git/wt-atlas-vector-backend`: 6,221 — divergent Atlas lineage, needs equivalence review, not assumed stranded.
- `~/git/fleet` (fleet repo clone): **1,556 dirty files** on main, no origin/main tracking ref — biggest single uncommitted pile.
- Small not-in-main commit counts (1–2) on ~10 queue worktrees, incl. `wt-id806` (design/id-806, #806 design work, Nov 1) and `devtoday-openchamber` queue/8357-224 (stale since Oct 22).
- Sandbox: no unpushed commits anywhere; one pushed-but-unmerged branch `docs/id-roadmap-phase14` (ID roadmap Phase 14 plan of record, epic #6312) in ~/git/devtoday-code; hatch-personal measured 0 ahead / 0 behind at 2026-11-08T02:52Z, contradicting Lane 4's 17:48 measurement of 244/45 — re-verify.

## Remainder (enqueued as queue tasks under this issue)
- Per-repo verification of the remaining ~5,036 closed issues (read-the-record standard; batched tranches of ~200).
- Full closed-unmerged PR verification (326).
- Local-branch full census without listing caps + patch-equivalence review for the stranded candidates; Atlas worktree equivalence; ~/git/fleet dirty-pile disposition review; hatch-personal divergence re-measurement.

Doctrine (Drew, 2026-11-07): triage completion never counts as done; this audit's tasks complete only with per-item evidence recorded.


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

items.body:
Parent: #2048 (ID Zettelkasten design). Phase 2 — depends on #3814 (stable note identity/revision graph).

Add structured references and a rebuildable local graph projection over the stable note model from #3814. A stored reference names a logical target note ID, the authored surface/sigil, and optionally a pinned revision ID. Derive outgoing topic links and backlinks from the selected revision heads; generic tags remain labels/aliases rather than directed edges. Provide deterministic local queries for a note's links/backlinks and topic chain.

Scope: local-store data model/index/query and tests. No editor or phrase-resolution UI, no cross-store fan-out, no global index, and no duplicate of the friendly-name candidate resolver/PoC owned by #2259. Do not start before #3814 has landed; if claimed early, park with that resume condition. Keep all search results within the store/view the caller is authorized to read.

Acceptance:
- Stored links use stable note IDs (optionally exact revision IDs); renames do not retarget them and the authored surface remains unchanged.
- Backlinks are a deterministic derived inverse of the selected revisions, not separately mutable canonical state.
- Concurrent note heads are represented explicitly; the query does not silently pick a head.
- A reference to inaccessible content exposes only its stored surface/unresolved state, not target content or private existence metadata.
- Tests cover duplicate names, rename, pinned revisions, concurrent heads, deterministic backlinks, and access-filtered results.

4. File a separate issue for every failure or gap found — do not fix-and-hide inside this task — and link them here.

**Exit:** every in-scope item is either verified by a passing test or has its own tracked issue; the full-suite results are recorded on this issue. Known starting point: ProseMirror revision replication to peers is an accepted gap (#792) — verify the rest of the brief still holds.
